transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-05-13
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Derek Shaw, Liam Ortiz (Redwood); Carlos Mendes, Priya Rao, Elena Voss, Samir Kaur (Arcadia)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly check-in for POC environment readiness and cutover planning.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Wednesday afternoon, appreciate it. Maya from Redwood here, joining with Derek and Liam. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Carlos Mendes: Hey Maya, doing good, busy week but we're on schedule.
[00:11] Priya Rao: Yeah, quick heads up, we just finished the VPC peering step in staging, but there's one last SG rule we need to verify.
[00:18] Elena Voss: We saw a couple of dropped packets in the first smoke test, might be an egress rule on our side.
[00:24] Derek Shaw: Okay that matches what we saw; when we ran the prefix caching test earlier today there was a small number of 503s during bursts, likely connection churn.
[00:33] Samir Kaur: We also wanted to confirm the plan for credential rotation — we don't want keys lingering in CI.
[00:40] Maya Chen: Totally. We can provide a temp key and then walk through SSO/SAML service account exchange. We'll also attach the secure onboarding doc after the call.
[00:48] Priya Rao: Perfect. On latency, when you say "connection churn" Derek, can you quantify? Our SLOs need p99 under 300ms ideally.
[00:56] Derek Shaw: Yeah, so in the synthetic runs we saw average token latency around 120ms but tail at p99 spiked to 540ms during a sustained burst at 200rps, so the average is good but the tail needs improving. Could be KV cache misses combined with cold workers.
[01:15] Carlos Mendes: Hmm, that p99 is worrysome, esp for our realtime recommendation paths. Any immediate recommendations?
[01:22] Liam Ortiz: One thing that helps is shortening our keepalive and adjusting the retry window on the gateway — we sent a sample NGINX config in the repo but we'll surface a playbook.
[01:30] Elena Voss: We're running with a 60s NAT timeout on the transit; if the worker IPs rotate that could cause new TLS handshakes.
[01:39] Derek Shaw: Yep, that aligns. Also consider pinning a small warm pool for critical routes during the cutover so cold starts are minimized.
[01:46] Priya Rao: Can Redwood do warm pool autoscaling? We may need extra cost visibility if we reserve capacity.
[01:52] Maya Chen: Yes we can recommend a reserved pool for the cutover window. We can show projected cost vs expected latency improvement in the console.
[01:59] Samir Kaur: On security, can you confirm SOC2 scope and whether audit logs will include per-request metadata?
[02:06] Maya Chen: We will include SOC2 summary in the packet. Audit logs capture request IDs and model version, not payloads unless you opt-in to a higher retention plan.
[02:14] Carlos Mendes: That's fine, we won't enable payload retention. We do need per-request latency and error codes in logs.
[02:19] Derek Shaw: We can forward a tracing hook that includes latency buckets and error tags.
[02:24] Priya Rao: Great. Next, about the synthetic tests — we'll run the 10k request burst tomorrow and share the results. The script will do ramp up and hold.
[02:33] Maya Chen: Perfect — if you can post the raw CSV we'll run our KV cache diagnostic while it's happening. Please include timestamps so we can align traces.
[02:42] Priya Rao: Will do. One question on fallbacks — in the event of model variant degradation, how does Redwood handle automatic fallback?
[02:50] Derek Shaw: We can route by policy: primary model, then lower-fidelity quantized variant. There's an auto-fallback that triggers on error rate thresholds. That said, we recommend canarying traffic and a rollback window.
[03:02] Elena Voss: And during the rollback, do you have a circuit breaker to stop sending traffic entirely?
[03:07] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we support circuit breakers per-route and you can set thresholds for error percentage and latency to trip to a safe mode.
[03:14] Carlos Mendes: Ok good. On operational ties, we need a clear rollback playbook — we can't be in a situation where production is degraded for 15+ minutes.
[03:21] Maya Chen: Understood, Derek we'll draft a cutover dry-run script and rollback checklist.
[03:26] Derek Shaw: I'll include steps: pre-checks, warm-pool sizing, traffic shift (% by minute), and rollback triggers.
[03:33] Priya Rao: About SSO exchange, Elena and I will need a sandbox identity provider metadata file. Does Redwood accept SAML or OIDC?
[03:41] Maya Chen: We support both; SAML for SSO and OIDC for service accounts. For the initial POC we recommend OIDC service account with short-lived tokens to avoid long-lived keys in CI.
[03:51] Elena Voss: We'll try OIDC then. I'll export metadata and send it to Maya.
[03:56] Samir Kaur: One last technical ask — during the earlier benchmark we saw KV cache thrash when sequence length varied a lot. Any suggestions?
[04:04] Derek Shaw: You can normalize prompt prefixes or use a prompt cache key strategy to group similar prefixes. Also quantization profiles that favor smaller activation sizes help reduce memory churn.
[04:15] Priya Rao: We'll test a prompt normalization pass as part of the synthetic script.
[04:19] Maya Chen: Great. Let's capture next steps and owners.
[04:22] [brief pause, cross talk]
[04:30] Maya Chen: Recap: Arcadia runs 10k synthetic test by Tuesday, Priya to share script and results; Elena to confirm VPC/Security group egress; Derek to share cutover/rollback playbook and sample NGINX; Maya to send onboarding and SOC2 summary. We'll tentatively plan a 30-minute dry-run next Friday after successful test.
[04:50] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood side that would prevent the dry-run?
[04:55] Maya Chen: No blockers from our side; just need the synthetic results and the SSO metadata file.
[05:00] Samir Kaur: Great, thanks everyone.
[05:02] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and the playbook. Bye.

--- End transcript ---
notes: Redwood will attach secure onboarding doc and SOC2 summary to CRM record
